title: Customer escalation war-room — Omega Retail (prep + notes)
content:
Meeting: Omega Retail escalation war-room (prep + live notes)
Date: 2026-03-11
Time: 11:00 PT / 19:00 UTC
Owner (doc): Aisha Patel
Goal: Triage P1 latency/regression impacting checkout embeddings pipeline; agree on mitigations, customer comms, and next steps.

Agenda:
- Quick context (2 min)
- Current impact & metrics (5 min)
- RCA hypothesis & data to collect (10 min)
- Immediate mitigations (fallbacks, traffic routing) (8 min)
- Customer communication cadence & template (5 min)
- Action items & owners (5 min)
- Schedule follow-up (2 min)

Participants:
- Aisha Patel (CS lead)
- Liam O'Connor (SRE)
- Sofia Martinez (Serving runtime eng)
- Rajiv Nair (Platform / routing)
- Emily Park (Tier 2 support on-call)
- Omega Retail: Michael Chen (Eng), Priya Rao (SRE), Joanna Li (PM)

Background / quick summary:
- 2026-03-10 22:10 UTC: Omega reports checkout timeouts and spikes. Symptoms correlate with embedding endpoint (POST /v1/embeddings) used by their recommenders.
- Customer impact: Checkout timeouts ~5-8% of sessions, increased cart abandonment. Customer rates as P1 (revenue impact).
- They are currently on hosted-api using model: text-embed-tilt-3 (quantized) via region us-west-2 with routing policy default -> hosted.
- Recent changes: 2026-03-09 automated rollout of small-quantization-profiles across embeddings fleet (linked: PR #4898). Suspect rollout introduced latency variance.

What we know so far (data pulled):
- 95th latency for embeddings for Omega tenant jumped from ~120ms to ~850ms starting 2026-03-10 21:50 UTC.
- Error rate remains low (<0.5%) but request queuing visible on the serving nodes (queued_request_count metric spiked).
- Affected nodes show higher GPU memory pressure and increased kernel fallback logs.
- Routing logs: Omega traffic was pinned to a dedicated pool with autoscale scaled down overnight; burst policies did not trigger as expected.

RCA hypotheses (working):
- Hypothesis A: Quantization profile rollout caused some model configurations to trigger slower execution kernels for certain sequence lengths.
- Hypothesis B: Autoscaler scaling policy mis-evaluated burst capacity due to incorrect utilization sampling window; pool under-provisioned.
- Hypothesis C: KV cache invalidation combined with cold start of many concurrent sessions created temporary load spike.

Data to collect now (owners):
- Pull serving runtime logs for embedding calls 21:30-22:30 UTC (Liam)
- Check autoscaler decisions & metrics for Omega pool 20:00-23:00 UTC (Rajiv)
- Verify model kernel selection traces and kernel fallback events (Sofia)
- Get tenant-specific token consumption + concurrency profile (Emily)

Immediate mitigations (decide during war-room):
- Short-term: Fail-open to smaller embed model (text-embed-mini) for Omega (customer approved?) - requires routing override + customer sign-off. Risk: quality drop. (Owner: Rajiv + Aisha)
- Short-term: Temporarily increase dedicated pool min capacity to handle current concurrency (Owner: Rajiv)
- Short-term: Rollback quantization profile for embeddings fleet (Owner: Sofia + release-eng) - high impact, coordinate with release window.
- Communication: Send status update to Omega within 30 minutes; include mitigation plan and expected ETA. Use template below. (Owner: Aisha)

Comms template (to customer):
- TL;DR: We see latency spikes impacting checkout; triaging and applying mitigations now. Next update in 30m.
- What we are doing: increasing capacity, investigating recent rollout, considering temporary fallback to smaller model.
- Impact: brief quality degradation possible if fallback used.
- Owner contact: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.com)

Notes to self / running checklist during meeting:
- Keep logs/screenshots of queued_request_count + GPU mem pressure.
- If we decide rollback, confirm exact release tag and rollback playbook steps.
- If fallback to smaller model, prepare a canary test with 5% traffic first.
- Confirm SLA credit process with finance (if escalation qualifies) - ping finance ops.

Post-meeting action items (captured live):
- Aisha: Send 30m status update to Omega + set customer expectation for next call. Due: 2026-03-11 11:30 PT.
- Rajiv: Temporarily increase pool min capacity to handle 2x current concurrency and monitor. Due: 2026-03-11 11:15 PT.
- Sofia: Gather kernel selection traces and confirm if quantization rollout correlates with performance regression (attach logs). Due: 2026-03-11 13:00 PT.
- Liam: Collect serving runtime logs 21:30-22:30 UTC and produce short timeline. Due: 2026-03-11 12:00 PT.
- Emily: Export tenant concurrency profile and current token backlog; surface any customer-side spikes. Due: 2026-03-11 12:00 PT.
- Release-eng (cc: Rajiv): Prepare rollback checklist for quantization profile; estimate risk and time to rollback. Due: 2026-03-11 14:00 PT.
- Aisha + Michael Chen (Omega): Decide on fallback to smaller model (customer approval). Due: 2026-03-11 12:00 PT.

Follow-ups / open questions:
- Did any other tenants see similar 95th latency increases after the rollout? (SRE telemetry query)
- Confirm if autoscaler sampling window change was deployed in last 7 days.
- If rollback is required, what is customer visibility plan (docs + impacts)?

Next meeting:
- Stand-up tomorrow 2026-03-12 11:00 PT to review RCA and final remediation.

Quick links / runbooks referenced:
- Embeddings performance playbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-performance
- Autoscaler diagnostics guide: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/autoscaler-diagnostics
- Relevant PR: repo/redwood/ops#4898 (quantization rollout)

Misc (scratchpad):
- If we increase pool capacity, watch cost impact and note in internal follow-up for billing team.
- Keep a log of customer-facing messages in Confluence page linked above.
- TODO: Create a short post-mortem template if incident remains >24h (owner: Aisha).

-- end of live notes --
